C01.why: Strongest validated demand on the slate: the anomaly-job pattern (Sell Fries! ~112K peak, 7 Days Cat-Sitting +825% wk40, licensed Exit 8) is rising, the format fits mobile and 28-day retention via chapters, and horror skews 13+/18+, where Roblox now pays more (R15 adult DevEx). Co-op roles are a real differentiator over the mostly solo incumbents. Not an 8 because by Mar 2027 the lane will be crowded with AI clones and Sell Fries will be on chapter 3–4.
C01.fix: Lead with the co-op role split (CCTV + patrol) in thumbnails and the name to avoid being demoted as a look-alike; budget the live-ops per chapter (new wing = ~20 anomalies) before committing; target a 13+ rating and skip Kids/Select at launch.
C01.biggest_risk: Arriving 5–6 months into a fast-cloning trend; each chapter's content cost is high while anomalies get consumed quickly.

C02.why: Novel on Roblox, and BOMBANANA proves the hook on Steam, but that hook depends on voice/text chaos that Roblox gates. Forcing exactly 3 players, often strangers, who communicate only through 8 emotes kills cold-start retention. Monetization is shallow (confetti cosmetics), with no collection or ownership pull.
C02.fix: Make the core 2-player and the 3-role mode optional, add a solo daily puzzle, and add a persistent sticker/device collection that cosmetics hang off.
C02.biggest_risk: Matchmade strangers cannot coordinate through icons alone, so D1 retention collapses and discovery never surfaces it.

C03.why: One-button input, a wide age range, kid-safe and highly clippable; the Fart Together takedown leaves a validated, clean lane open and Backseat Rally shows role-split co-op traction. Cheap to extend (courses, vehicles), but novelty-driven chaos games historically spike and fade, and depth for 28-day retention is thin.
C03.fix: Build a deeper meta (vehicle collection with layouts, weekly ranked course, friend ghosts) and plan a vehicle-of-the-month cadence; get Kids/Select eligibility early because this is the most under-13-friendly concept.
C03.biggest_risk: Viral-then-gone curve: a strong first week with no retention backbone, and quick copies by bigger studios.

C04.why: Shop-sim progression is native to Roblox's tycoon-loving audience and Probably Stolen (660K demo players) validates the inspect-and-haggle hook; it is mobile-friendly and has collection (museum) monetization surfaces. But co-op is optional, the detective depth is hard to keep fresh without heavy authoring, and Probably Stolen clones will appear.
C04.fix: Make rare-item collection the long-term spine (seasonal 'treasure sets'), make Forger Night the social/viral mode, and keep inspection under 20 seconds on mobile.
C04.biggest_risk: Reads as yet another shop tycoon in a falling simulator category and gets demoted alongside them.

C05.why: The most marketable hook on the slate ('hide the mess before Mom gets home') works for kids and YouTubers, the asymmetric 1vN format is proven on Roblox (MM2, Flee the Facility), there are no pay-to-win needs, and the Parent role drives role-swap replays and friend invites. Steam signals (No Body No Problem!, Worst Class Ever) are fresh.
C05.fix: Lock down physics netcode on low-end mobile early (cap physics objects), ship 2 houses at launch with a new-house-per-month cadence, and pursue Kids/Select eligibility since the theme is child-native.
C05.biggest_risk: Physics-heavy server sync on mobile at 7 players; if it lags or desyncs, the comedy dies and so does retention.

C06.why: A clever shared-pile hook, but it is fundamentally an incremental/tycoon in a category Roblox is demoting (simulators falling, anti 'cash-grabby' stance), and it monetizes via boosts, which invites FTC/policy scrutiny. Find the Needle's demo peak is small (~8.6K).
C06.fix: Make it a weekly event mode inside a bigger game, or replace boosts with cosmetic machines only and add competitive needle races between servers.
C06.biggest_risk: Lost in a sea of tycoons and penalized for idle/boost loops.

C07.why: Chained Together already had its Roblox clone wave in 2024 and the PEAK-like SUMMIT peaks at only ~1K CCU, a weak signal that Roblox players want this. Rope physics plus climbing on a mobile thumbstick is high-risk and frustrating, and PEAK hype will be 18+ months old by launch.
C07.fix: Only pursue if a prototype makes mobile climbing feel great in week 2; otherwise drop it. Consider the 'Summit Stream' spectacle twist for differentiation.
C07.biggest_risk: Mobile controls feel bad, and the genre reads as a stale 2024 obby trend.

C08.why: Co-op horror is healthy, the 'views' scoring gives a shareable, streamer-friendly twist, and the replay montage is a built-in social hook. It is likely contested by existing Content-Warning-likes (unverified), and the tagged-moment montage is technical scope a small team may underestimate.
C08.fix: Verify the Roblox competition now; scope the montage as tagged-event highlight cards (not camera replays); add a weekly 'trending ghost' to drive return visits.
C08.biggest_risk: The differentiating feature (the montage) is the costliest to build well, and without it the game is a generic ghost hunt.

C09.why: Fresh input on Roblox, and wave defence monetizes well, but the tower-defence space is dominated by heavy hitters with unit-gacha economies. Gesture recognition accuracy on small phones and with a mouse on PC is a real UX risk, and spell combos need coordination that strangers rarely achieve.
C09.fix: Prototype gesture accuracy on low-end phones first; add a rune-book collection plus seasonal schools of magic as the retention spine; offer simplified tap-cast as a fallback.
C09.biggest_risk: Input frustration on mobile (55–80% of sessions) turns a novelty into churn.

C10.why: Pets and breeding are perennial Roblox money-makers, inheritance has a strong long-term pull (fits 28-day retention), and monetization (nest slots) scales. But scope is high (roguelite + auto-battle + genetics + balance), co-op is bolted on, and it sits near crowded pet-sim/gacha-TD lanes.
C10.fix: Cut the battle layer to a very simple auto-battler and invest in trading or friend cross-breeding as the viral/social engine; avoid paid randomness disclosure issues by keeping mutations earned.
C10.biggest_risk: Too much system design for 3–4 months; launches thin and is out-competed by polished pet games.

C11.why: The liminal/extraction theme is hot (DONT SPLASH ~10M visits/day, R.E.P.O.) and appeals to the older audience, but DONT SPLASH's visits-to-CCU ratio signals short sessions, liminal obbies are saturated, and procedural extraction content is expensive to keep scary.
C11.fix: Differentiate with a hook (e.g. noise-only entity with a strong carry-physics comedy layer) and a persistent hub/museum; aim for 13+.
C11.biggest_risk: Indistinguishable from dozens of liminal/backrooms games already in discovery.

C12.why: Backseat Rally (28–55K peak) proves role-split co-op can gain traction now, and the airplane theme is broadly appealing. But it is very close to an emerging incumbent that can add aircraft itself, and three asymmetric roles with stranger matchmaking have the same coordination problem as C02.
C12.fix: Ship 2-player viability and a strong solo-with-bots mode; differentiate with vehicle variety (airship, sub) from day 1.
C12.biggest_risk: Positioned as 'Backseat Rally with planes' — a follower in a lane the leader can expand into.

C13.why: OpenFront-style games have a real niche, and clans/seasons are a durable, monetizable meta skewing older, but 50-player lobbies need high CCU to fill on a shrinking platform with a 28-day cold start. The map/strategy UI is hard on phones and the audience is niche on Roblox.
C13.fix: Use 12–20 player maps with bot fill, plus clan wars as the retention core; validate demand with a cheap prototype ad test first.
C13.biggest_risk: Cold start: empty or bot-filled lobbies at launch mean no retention signal and no discovery.

C14.why: A charming, streamable physics-comedy premise that is broadly age-appropriate, but it combines two expensive systems (driving + physics carrying) and delivery sims already exist on Roblox. Retention depth beyond novelty is unclear.
C14.fix: Drop driving (teleport/auto-route) and focus on the carry gauntlet; add weekly neighbourhoods and a rare-parcel collection.
C14.biggest_risk: Scope bloat; it ships late and floaty on mobile.

C15.why: Merge auto-battlers monetize well (battle pass, collection) and suit Roblox's unit-collecting kids, and ranked drives retention. But 8-player lobbies need fill, balance is a live-ops treadmill, and bigger TD/unit games sit adjacent; a competitive game also has nothing to sell beyond cosmetics without becoming pay-to-win.
C15.fix: Allow bot-fill, design 4-player quick mode, and keep the collection earned with cosmetic monetization to stay policy-safe.
C15.biggest_risk: Balance and content upkeep outpace a 2–5 person team.

C16.why: A weaker variant of 7 Days Cat-Sitting: it drops the anomaly twist that made that game grow, leaving a generic chore loop, and Animal Hospital-style games already serve the cozy lane. Rewarded video is a thin revenue model.
C16.fix: Merge into C01's anomaly structure or add a distinctive twist; otherwise drop it.
C16.biggest_risk: No reason to choose it over the incumbent it imitates.

C17.why: A thin loop with low monetization surface (piece skins), and the stacking genre is easy to clone and lightly differentiated. Turn-based placement makes for slow group play on Roblox.
C17.fix: Only as a minigame inside a bigger party product.
C17.biggest_risk: Low retention ceiling; a week-one novelty with nothing to buy.

C18.why: A memorable pitch, but Roblox servers are ephemeral and players hop between them, so 'your server's monster' needs cross-server persistence and community scale this team won't have at launch. The weekly payoff is too slow for D1/D7 signals, and the concept is under-specified.
C18.fix: Reframe as clan/group-owned monsters with daily mini-battles, and validate the fantasy with a cheap prototype.
C18.biggest_risk: The cold-start community never reaches critical mass, so the core fantasy never happens.

C19.why: Hide-in-plain-sight has proven demand (Worst Class Ever #1 Next Fest; Be NPC or Die on Roblox), and the museum/statue theme is kid-friendly and streamable. But it is a crowded sub-genre where differentiation is mostly thematic, and the 1-Guard role bottleneck can sour lobbies.
C19.fix: Lean into the shared Mischief objective as the distinctive layer, rotate museums monthly, and make the Guard role fun with gadgets.
C19.biggest_risk: Perceived as another Be NPC or Die clone and demoted as a look-alike.

C20.why: Head-on against Volleyball Legends, an entrenched Roblox incumbent, with only a control-scheme difference; sports competitors need scale for matchmaking, and the concept has no meta or hook.
C20.biggest_risk: Zero differentiation against an established leader.

overall_notes: Skeptical frame: Roblox DAU is down 9% YoY, bookings are down 12% and creator median earnings are ~$1,500/yr, so the base rate for a 4–6 month small-team bet is poor. Discovery now rewards 28-day retention and co-play, demotes look-alikes and penalizes cash-grab loops. Only C01 (validated anomaly-job trend + co-op differentiation + chapter cadence) and C05 (most marketable, kid/YouTuber-native asymmetric hook) reach a 7, and neither is an 8: C01 faces trend-lateness and clones; C05 faces mobile physics-netcode risk. Tier 2 (6): C03, C04 and C08 have real hooks but weak retention spines or scope traps. Concepts that depend on strangers coordinating through icons (C02, C12) or on large lobbies filling (C13, C15, C18) carry a cold-start risk that is lethal on a shrinking platform. Steam-hit adaptations (C02, C04, C07, C09) will race AI-assisted clones to Roblox, so being early matters more than polish. Recommendation: prototype C01 and C05 in parallel for 2–3 weeks with retention gates (D1 ≥ 25%, session ≥ 12 min), then commit.
